# Knowledge Base Memories

## No Co-Authored-By trailers in commits

Never add `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailers to commit messages. The user explicitly rejected this.

## Verify the current git branch before planning

Always run `git branch --show-current` at the start of a task — the conversation-start gitStatus may be stale if the user switched branches.

## Skip running tests during code review

During code review (e.g. /review-changes), do NOT run the test suite — assume tests pass. Focus on diff reading for correctness, design, ticket fit.

## Prefer structured lists over wide markdown tables

Don't render comparisons as wide multi-column tables — they wrap and misalign in terminal/IDE. Use bullet lists instead.

## Drafting a PR/MR is not permission to create one

Never run `glab/gh ... create` unless the user explicitly says to create the MR/PR. Drafting a title+description (e.g. /create-pr) is output-only — stop there.

## Ask the user to run tests after 2 opaque attempts

After 2 attempts where test output is opaque (hung, truncated, no real error), stop guessing — ask the user to run the command and paste output.

## Delegate to a subagent after 2 failed test-setup attempts

After 2 failed test-setup attempts on the same blocker (locator/flow), stop guessing — spawn a subagent to investigate (dump DOM, map path), then apply once.

## Uncommitted changes onto latest master = new branch + stash-pop

Uncommitted changes onto latest master: `git stash` → `checkout -b <new> origin/master` → `stash pop`. Don't rebase. Never `-X ours/theirs` — corrupts files.

## Link files at their actual worktree path, not the main checkout

When linking files on a worktree/feature branch, prefix with the worktree dir (e.g. `repo-TICKET-123/`), not the main checkout dir. Otherwise the IDE link is dead.

## Check package.json (or equivalent) for the project's test command

Always check `package.json` scripts (or equivalent) for the project's test command. Don't run raw `jest`/`vitest`/`pytest` — the npm script wraps env loading and exit flags.

## Concise comments, no ticket IDs

Code/test comments must be skimmable (typically one line, WHY-focused). Never include ticket IDs in source comments — they belong in commit messages / MRs, not the code.

## 2+ defensible behaviors → stop and ask the user

When a code path has 2+ defensible behaviors (lossy vs preserve, gate vs skip, fail-closed vs fail-open), stop and ask the user — overrides 'don't stop for review'.

## "could/can you" = a request → act. "could/can we" = a question → answer and recommend, do not act yet.

"could/can you" = a request → act. "could/can we" = a question → answer and recommend, do not act yet.

## On substantive multi-step work, run ai-kanban-track-session: open an in_progress card (tags=.ai-rules.json scope, +sessionId), append progress, set need_review when done. Skip trivial tasks.

On substantive multi-step work, run ai-kanban-track-session: open an in_progress card (tags=.ai-rules.json scope, +sessionId), append progress, set need_review when done. Skip trivial tasks.

## User says 'won't fix' / 'fixed' / 'invalid' (or similar short phrase) → post that exact phrase verbatim as the comment body. No lead-in, no rationale. Explain only if asked.

User says 'won't fix' / 'fixed' / 'invalid' (or similar short phrase) → post that exact phrase verbatim as the comment body. No lead-in, no rationale. Explain only if asked.

## Sub-agents: never Read generated/large files

Never let sub-agents Read generated/large files (codegen output, lockfiles, big fixtures) — regenerate via codegen. Each read permanently bloats agent context.

## Don't hand-edit AI-rules-repo dogfood copies

In AI-rules-repo, never manually edit .claude/skills/ dogfood copies — they're regenerated by the CLI (sync/init). Edit the source under skills/<agent>/ only.

## Fable 5 only on explicit request, per-prompt

Use Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) only when the user explicitly asks; that request applies to that prompt ONLY and never carries to later turns. Default everything else to the normal model.

## When a user-requested MCP/tool is unavailable, STOP, announce it, and ask for next step. Never work around it (WebFetch/curl/guessing) — the user will reconnect; then retry.

When a user-requested MCP/tool is unavailable, STOP, announce it, and ask for next step. Never work around it (WebFetch/curl/guessing) — the user will reconnect; then retry.

## Write skimmable bullets

When writing bullets/plans/technical-design, make them skimmable: lead with the point (bold subject), one idea per bullet, ~1 line, no wall-of-text.

## Inline step comments over top block

For non-trivial SQL/code, prefer a short comment on each step/clause over one large explanatory block at the top (one-line intro at most) — the reader understands each piece in place.

## Never git add -A; stage explicit paths

Never `git add -A`/`-a`/`.`; stage explicit paths and verify `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` first. cwd drifts between nested repos — a blanket add once staged a private key in the wrong repo.

## Explain a valid review comment from zero context

Explaining a valid review comment: assume zero code knowledge — name each moving piece, the rule that makes them collide, a timeline, then blast radius and if a fix is a judgment call.

## No newspaper-headline section titles

Never write headline-style section titles (verdict + em-dash). Use plain descriptive headings. Bad: 'A second, older fault - 3 sites'. Good: 'Other failures found in earlier months'.

## Explain assuming the user knows nothing about the project

When explaining work or asking the user to decide, assume zero project knowledge — define the terms and give each option's concrete consequence. Jargon blocks a real decision.

## Introspect columns before querying an unfamiliar table

Before querying an unfamiliar table, run information_schema.columns first. Guessing names (user vs abstract_user, user_id vs "userId") burns round trips.

## Slack read access via ~/.slack-bot-token

Read Slack via Web API with the bot token in ~/.slack-bot-token (conversations.replies + users.info, Bearer). Never echo it. Permalink p<digits> -> ts: dot 6 digits from end.

## DB check requested → must actually query the DB

User asks to check the DB: if it's unreachable, STOP and report — never substitute code-reading for real data.

## No assert for type validation in TS

Never use assert() for type or shape validation in TS. Validate external input (config, payloads) with a named Zod schema; assert is only for genuine runtime invariants.
